idea: Charged circulation on repeated, spatially connected xy/xz compact electric faces creates real intercell flux-current mixing without supplied magnetic B². A local gauge-invariant field impulse now reaches a disjoint face two cells away, with delayed response and electric-energy transfer; a literal Wilson/CAR charge source also moves through the same dynamic electric-link law. This is useful finite spatial propagation, not a relabelled pair of local poles, not a Bloch dispersion, and not an established massless photon phase.
backward_path: Start from the unmet target: spatial electromagnetic field transport in two directions transverse to a common propagation axis, coupled to actual charge motion.
Repeat the frozen two-face mechanism into a shared-x-spine ladder with charged y and z outer rails; every neighboring cell is connected through physical links and charged hopping.
Retain ordinary integer electric spectra, exact local Gauss, spinful CAR, Hubbard interaction and all retained joint field/matter states; add no plaquette cosine or B² restoring law.

Use an explicitly finite local electric-link domain |E_e|<=1 on every link. Because open ends and static integer ions break translations, measure real-space/full-H time response instead of inventing momentum.
Execute Nc=1,2,3 with one parameter set, then materially remove circulating rail hopping and all matter motion as adverse mechanisms; keep primitive E² throughout.

Prepare a new local unitary sine-Wilson pulse on the induced joint ground and a separate actual one-charge tree-Wilson/CAR source on the empty sector; propagate each under its disclosed full Hamiltonian.

failed_forks_and_discriminators.long_distance_strength: Nc3 coherence decreases to .01722 on cell2 and flux propagation amplitude to .03854. Localized ionic ground does not provide a uniform strong electromagnetic medium; this surviving finite mechanism is not evidence of a macroscopic propagating photon phase.
